name: PNB Housing Finance Ltd
title: PNB Housing Finance Ltd - 540173 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Housing finance with no capacity signal; spread fell 10 bps to 2.12% on yield cuts, GNPA 0.93% and negative credit cost carry FY27 ROA guide of 2.4-2.5% (down from 2.66%).

summary.headline: PNB Housing Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores; FY27 guidance is loan book above INR 1 lakh crore and ROA 2.4-2.5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 36% YoY and 50% QoQ to INR 9,355 crores, with retail disbursements up 32% YoY to INR 9,020 crores. PAT rose 19% YoY to INR 656 crores in Q4 and 18% to INR 2,291 crores for FY26, helped by negative credit cost of 45 bps from write-off pool recoveries. Spread compressed 10 bps QoQ to 2.12% on lower incremental yields and balance transfer pressure in Prime, while reported NIM rose 6 bps to 3.69%. Management guided that yields have bottomed out, with FY27 retail loan growth of 18-20%, NIM of 3.55-3.65% and ROA of 2.4-2.5%.

financial_highlights.change: -15 bps QoQ; FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% in FY25
+13% YoY; opex to ATA 1.05% FY26, 1.08% Q4
Recoveries INR 167 crores in Q4, INR 330-332 crores in FY26

segments.name: Affordable
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursement INR 1,249 crores, up 59% QoQ but flat YoY; FY26 disbursement about INR 3,800 crores, targeted to grow about 50%. Management says GNPA in affordable is below 0.6%.

segments.name: Emerging Market
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 34% YoY in Q4. Segment share of retail loan book rose with affordable plus emerging at 40% of retail book (37% a year earlier).

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 43% YoY in Q4 despite yield pressure from rate cuts. Management says Prime disbursement largely replenishes runoff; Prime loan growth is about 9%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Restarted with INR 335 crores disbursed in Q4 FY26; corporate loan book INR 401 crores at 31 March 2026. Target yield 11.5-12%, capped at about 3% of book in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Loan book to cross INR 1 lakh crore in FY27.
Retail loan book growth of 18-20% in FY27; overall book growth stated as 18-20%.
NIM guided at 3.55-3.65% for FY27; management expects spread-NIM gap to normalise from Q1 FY27.
Credit cost expected to stay negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with recoveries of INR 200-250 crores.
Opex to ATA expected to stay in a 1-1.1% range; cost of borrowing stable or 5-10 bps better.
Affordable and emerging to reach about 50% of the book in two to three years; corporate to reach 5-6% in year two and 8-9% in year three.
capex_capacity: Opened 35 branches in Q4 FY26, taking the network to 393 branches (229 affordable, 87 emerging market).
Management said the priority is to make existing branches more productive rather than adding many more.
Infinity in-house digital onboarding app is fully adopted by the in-house sales team; direct selling agents are being onboarded.
Digital channels generate about 15% of leads.
Micro LAP and micro housing products planned for launch in Q1 FY27 in the 14-16% yield segment.
demand_pricing: Management cited intense pricing competition, especially in Q4, and said affordable yield fell about 75 bps QoQ to as low as 11.35%.
Balance transfer (BT) out was 8.6% in Q4 FY26 vs 8.95% in Q3 and 8% for FY26.
Industry housing finance growth cited at 12-13%; the company describes itself as third-largest in the industry.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose to 7.23% in Q4 from 7.2% in Q3 amid current liquidity conditions.
Non-housing share of the book at 32.4% vs 30.6% in Q3; PBC retail home loans at 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the spread fall while NIM rose, and will the ROA gap normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said the divergence is a methodology difference (daily spread convention vs monthly NIM averaging) and should normalise from next quarter, with NIM in a 5-10 bps range of current trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost is built into the 2.4-2.5% ROA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said credit cost is expected to remain negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with write-off pool recoveries continuing; mix shift to emerging, affordable and corporate should support NIM over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did affordable disbursements weaken and is it linked to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said affordable disbursements rebounded in Q4, mid-year challenges were temporary and fixed, and quality is not the reason; Prime disbursement reflects replenishment of runoff.

qa_highlights.question: What early bounce and stress indicators are visible for April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April bounce rates are similar to March, with no significant jump; a one-off government-employee EMI bounce was cleared the next day.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident yields have bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said no repo change in recent months, so balance transfer outflows should restrict, supporting yield; BT out improved from Q3 to Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR 335 crore corporate disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one case in FY26 was about INR 360-370 crores, primarily in Mumbai; focus is on reputed builders in about seven or eight top cities, with corporate at about 3% of book in FY27.

risks_watch: Yield recovery depends on balance transfer outflows staying restricted and on no further rate cuts; management also flagged possible upside in market rates.
Credit cost is negative because of write-off pool recoveries (about INR 500 crores corporate and INR 325 crores retail remaining); normalisation could weigh on ROA.
Opex grew 13% and the full cost of 35 Q4 branches will flow into FY27; opex to ATA target 1-1.1%.
Cost of borrowing: management expects only stable to 5-10 bps improvement; a rating upgrade is being pursued as a lever.
Geopolitical and crude-oil risk could affect inflation, rates and asset quality, though management sees no early stress as of mid-April.
Prime 30+ DPD on a like-for-like basis is 2.72% (investor presentation figure of 3.31% includes Stage-2 SICR accounts).
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, disbursement recovery and asset quality, with the yield-bottoming call supported by balance transfer trends. Cautious on cost of borrowing, which management says has limited room to fall, and it was hedged on geopolitical risk. Some answers on the Q4 spread-NIM divergence and the 30+ DPD figures needed clarification.
key_quotes: We are looking for loan book to cross more than INR 1 lakh crores mark in FY'27.
In our view, the yield have bottomed out and should start improving from Q1 FY'27.
The mantra would be growth with quality.
Affordable has started shaping up now.

adds.what: 35 branches opened in Q4 FY26, network at 393 branches (229 affordable, 87 emerging market); management prioritising productivity over adding many more branches
Micro LAP and micro housing products planned for launch in Q1 FY27 (14-16% yield segment)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of retail loan book growth 18-20% and total book above INR 1 lakh crore (about 15% growth from INR 87,347 crore), with ROA 2.4-2.5%; backed by Q4 disbursements up 36% YoY and 35 branch openings, but no quantified capacity or order book behind the growth, and management cited intense pricing competition and falling affordable yields.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Yield on loans fell 25 bps QoQ to 9.47% and spread fell 10 bps to 2.12%, but management expects yields to have bottomed (BT out 8.6% in Q4 vs 8.95% in Q3) and the spread-NIM gap to normalise, while FY27 NIM guidance of 3.55-3.65% is below the Q4 reported 3.69%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network grew to 393 branches after 35 openings in Q4 FY26, but management prioritises productivity of existing branches over adding many more, so further openings are not guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores, and FY27 guidance is retail book growth of 18-20% (FY26 retail book INR 86,946 crores, +16% YoY), backed by affordable and emerging disbursement momentum.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is set at new levels (book above INR 1 lakh crore, NIM 3.55-3.65%, ROA 2.4-2.5%) with intense pricing competition and falling yields, leaving little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost is negative at -45 bps in FY26 only because write-off pool recoveries (INR 330-332 crores) are flowing; guidance assumes -15 to -20 bps, and affordable yield fell about 75 bps QoQ to 11.35%, with cost of borrowing at 7.35% in Q4 and only 5-10 bps improvement expected.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Micro LAP and micro housing products are planned for launch in Q1 FY27 in the 14-16% yield segment, with no size quantified.

rows.label: Corporate book capped at about 3% in FY27
rows.why: Corporate book was INR 401 crores at 31 March 2026, restarted with INR 335 crores disbursed in Q4 FY26, with a target yield of 11.5-12% and cap at about 3% of book.

rows.label: Cost of borrowing 5-10 bps better, rating upgrade pursued
rows.why: Cost of borrowing is 7.35% in Q4 (FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% FY25), management guides only stable to 5-10 bps better and says a rating upgrade is a lever; incremental cost rose to 7.23% from 7.2%.

rows.label: Yield bottoming on restricted balance transfer outflows
rows.why: BT out fell to 8.6% in Q4 from 8.95% in Q3 with no repo change recently, but intense affordable pricing competition (affordable yield 11.35%) and rate-cut risk remain.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement recovery, asset quality (GNPA 0.93%) and yield bottoming, but cautious on cost of borrowing and hedged on geopolitical risk; analysts probed the Q4 spread-NIM divergence, the Prime 30+ DPD figures and the sustainability of negative credit cost.
